subject: codebuff
title: Compaction fires opportunistically only when the provider prompt cache has demonstrably gone cold
one_why: Measures the idle gap last-assistant -> live user prompt; only past the TTL does it rewrite history, because the next request re-reads the whole history uncached anyway, so the rewrite is free -- plus a min-tokens floor so small contexts are never compacted for nothing, which the must-fire context-limit trigger deliberately ignores. Independent convergence with gptme's TTL cold-cache prediction.

subject: codebuff
title: Model handoff -> mechanical pass -> leave-unchanged ladder; a compaction failure can never fail the user's turn
evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts:316-384 (compactWithModelOrFallback), :71-98 (base64-eliding JSON replacer), :200-225 (binary-search budget fit); compact-history.ts:701-841 (no-LLM budgeted mechanical pass)
one_why: Preferred LLM summarizer with map-reduce chunking and screenshot-elision (a documented 800k-token incident fix), falling back to a zero-model mechanical rewrite that keeps every file read/edited and command run, then to honest no-op with an over-budget guard; the old design returned full history on failure and left context over budget, and the comment records why it changed.

subject: codebuff
title: Two-stage unchanged-todo breaker whose recovery note knows which tools the agent actually has
one_why: Three consecutive identical write_todos calls inject targeted recovery guidance, six end the turn with a user-facing error; when no file-edit tool is offered (plan mode) the injected note says so explicitly, because a stuck model kept 'calling' write_file under the name of the nearest available tool.

subject: codebuff
title: Dual trust gates: inventoried .agents-dir prompt before any repo code import or MCP spawn, publisher allowlist before eval'd remote handleSteps
one_why: Trust prompt first shows WHAT loading would do (agent file list, MCP launch commands); store is realpath-keyed 0600, non-interactive runs skip rather than silently trust; remote executable templates were 'RCE by design' until the publisher gate, and the residual gaps (no signing, unpinned latest, unsandboxed eval) are named as deliberate scope limits rather than hidden.

subject: codebuff
title: Advertiser-authored sponsored runs execute locally under seatbelt/bubblewrap with refuse-never-downgrade semantics
one_why: One seatbelt profile and one bwrap arglist in the repo, behind a broker interface chosen so a future sandbox-exec removal is a swap not a rewrite; HOME redirected AND real one denied, loopback denied (the orchestrator listens there), symlink-aware write containment; a missing bwrap throws instead of spawning uncontained -- and the gap inventory deliberately does not ship to the public repo.

subject: codebuff
title: Capability grant is computed from measured containment, with Windows's unsandboxed 'floor' as its own type, grant, and env
one_why: sponsoredLocalGrant(platform, containment) is a function, never a bare constant -- so run_commands is grantable only where the kernel boundary exists, and the Windows floor cannot be mistaken for a sandbox because it is a distinct arm with distinct types; 'one constant per environment, not one shared constant with a comment'.

subject: codebuff
title: 151,832 LOC of behavior-asserting tests that the public CI never runs -- CI is build + binary smoke only
one_why: The corpus is real (loop semantics, cancellation, sandbox profiles, cross-artifact parity) and carefully runnable credential-free, but the only public workflow builds and smokes; docs/testing.md's claim 'CI runs cd <package> && bun test' describes the private tree, so a public contributor's green mirror proves nothing; no evals (BuffBench) or fuzzing in CI either.

subject: codebuff
title: General agent path has no approval, no sandbox, and project-escaping file writes by design, with no public statement of either
evidence: sdk/src/tools/path-utils.ts:43-68 (resolveFilePath honors 'any file on the system'); grep approval/needsApproval/autoApprove = 0 hits in sdk/src/run.ts and packages/agent-runtime; SECURITY.md (7-line contact boilerplate); only undo is /ads:undo (cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts:282)
one_why: The impressive enforcement is all out-of-band (sponsored runs, trust gates, SSRF) while everyday file edits and bash run unconstrained on the user's machine -- fine as a design choice, but unlike pi's exemplary 'intentionally does not have a sandbox' SECURITY.md, the public materials neither claim nor disclaim protection, which reads as a control that is not there.

subject: codebuff
title: Steering queue drained exactly at step boundaries, appending user prompts and forcing the turn to continue
one_why: Host-fed messages land only after the step's LLM call and tools complete, so history is in a clean state -- steering neither aborts the in-flight step nor interrupts mid-tool-batch, and any steered text reopens a turn that was about to end; convergent with gptme's durable steer queue, different delivery point.

subject: codebuff
title: Context size = last provider receipt plus string-length deltas, never re-tokenizing; recount even on failed and cancelled turns
one_why: Anchors on the real usage receipt per model, adjusts only for content added since (model switch invalidates the anchor), so the user's context meter stays truthful through aborts and history edits at near-zero tokenization cost -- the receipts are also gated on history identity so a set_messages rewrite cannot inherit a stale baseline (run-agent-step.ts:600-620).
